title: Weakly interacting Bose-Einstein condensate with stochastic resetting
authors: Nikhil Mesquita, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar, Sanjib Sabhapandit
abstract: Stochastic resetting can generate strong correlations in many-body systems through a shared fluctuating environment. Here, we investigate how such dynamically emergent correlations (DEC) coexist with intrinsic (direct) interactions in a weakly repulsive Bose-Einstein condensate described within the Gross-Pitaevskii framework. The condensate undergoes free expansion from an initial Thomas-Fermi state and is stochastically reset to this initial state at a constant rate. We show that the resetting protocol drives the system into a unique nonequilibrium steady state and obtain its density profile, edge statistics, and full counting statistics analytically. The steady-state density retains an inverted-parabolic form within the core, while developing exponentially decaying tails outside it. We further show that resetting induces nontrivial fluctuations of the condensate edge and particle number, yielding exact scaling forms for the edge distribution and the full counting statistics. Our results provide a tractable setting for exploring the interplay between intrinsic repulsive interactions and attractive DEC generated by a common stochastic environment in quantum many-body systems.
summary: This work analyzes a weakly interacting Bose-Einstein condensate subjected to stochastic resetting, which introduces dynamically emergent correlations. The authors derive the non-equilibrium steady state properties, finding a specific density profile and exact scaling forms for particle number fluctuations. This study offers insight into how external noise can fundamentally alter the many-body physics of quantum gases.
main_problem: The paper investigates how dynamically emergent correlations (DEC) generated by stochastic resetting interact with intrinsic repulsive interactions in a Bose-Einstein condensate.
main_result: The system reaches a unique non-equilibrium steady state characterized by a density profile with an inverted-parabolic core and exponentially decaying tails, alongside nontrivial fluctuations in edge and particle number.
method: The analysis involves solving the Gross-Pitaevskii equation in the mean-field limit and analytically computing observables like density profiles and full counting statistics in the steady state.
model_or_system: The system is a weakly interacting Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) of bosons confined in a highly elongated harmonic trap, modeled using the Gross-Pitaevskii framework.
key_observables: Steady-state density profile, edge statistics, and full counting statistics.
important_parameters: Stochastic resetting rate ($r$), interaction strength ($g$), and the system size/length scales.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes weak repulsive interactions and utilizes the Thomas-Fermi approximation for the initial state.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the analysis focuses on deriving analytical forms for the density profile and the distribution function $H(\kappa)$ for the counting statistics.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the model, analyzing the free expansion dynamics, and finally deriving the steady-state properties under the stochastic resetting protocol.
why_interesting: It provides a tractable theoretical framework to study the competition between mean-field repulsive interactions and non-local, attractive correlations induced by external fluctuating environments (stochastic resetting).
